title: Ghana’s mobile-money system is scaling rapidly while active-agent capacity and oversight remain critical constraints
source_unit: Bank of Ghana, Payment Systems Oversight Annual Report 2024
geography: Ghana; national payment-system and fintech administrative indicators, with mobile-money, banking-channel, agent, licensing, financial-inclusion, and oversight dimensions

denominator.unit: Bank of Ghana administrative payment-system reporting; transaction counts and values are system totals, not unique-person consumer observations

mobile_money_transaction_value_2024.unit: Ghana cedi billions in mobile-money transaction value in 2024

mobile_money_transaction_value_2023.unit: Ghana cedi billions in mobile-money transaction value in 2023

mobile_money_transaction_value_growth.unit: percent growth in mobile-money transaction value from 2023 to 2024

mobile_money_transaction_volume_growth.unit: percent growth in mobile-money transaction volume from 2023 to 2024

internet_banking_value_growth.unit: percent growth in internet-banking transaction value from 2023 to 2024

mobile_banking_value_growth.unit: percent growth in mobile-banking transaction value from 2023 to 2024

mechanism.value: Ghana’s payment infrastructure is becoming a high-frequency consumer and household-service layer, with mobile money carrying many low-value transactions while bank and instant-payment channels grow in value faster

observations.method: Bank of Ghana administrative system totals and year-on-year comparisons for mobile money, internet banking, and mobile banking transactions.
observations.uncertainty: Administrative transactions are not unique users, household purchases, cultural consumption, or welfare; values may include transfers, cash-in/cash-out, business activity, and repeated transactions.
observations.subgroup: Ghanaian payment-system users and institutions represented in national administrative reporting.
observations.counterinterpretation: Transaction growth may reflect inflation, repeat use, transfers, business flows, or system reclassification rather than equivalent growth in consumer purchasing power or inclusion.

denominator.unit: Bank of Ghana mobile-money ecosystem indicators; registered customers are cumulative accounts, active customers transacted within the prior 90 days, and active agents transacted within the prior 30 days

registered_mobile_money_customers_2024.unit: million cumulative registered mobile-money customers at end-2024

active_mobile_money_customers_2024.unit: million mobile-money customers active under the report’s 90-day definition at end-2024

active_customer_share_of_registered.unit: percent, calculated as active customers divided by registered customers; not a unique-person activation rate

registered_agents_2023.unit: thousand cumulative registered mobile-money agents at end-2023

active_agents_2023.unit: thousand active mobile-money agents at end-2023

active_agents_2024.unit: thousand active mobile-money agents at end-2024

active_agent_change.unit: percent change in active agents from 2023 to 2024, associated by the report with platform clean-up of fraudulent agents

mechanism.value: The payment network’s usable capacity depends on active customers and active cash-in/cash-out agents, not registered accounts alone; fraud clean-up can improve integrity while temporarily reducing local transaction access

observations.method: Bank of Ghana DEMI/mobile-money administrative indicators; active-customer and active-agent definitions are the report’s 90-day and 30-day activity windows, respectively.
observations.uncertainty: Registered accounts and agents can include duplicates, dormant entities, or multiple accounts; the active-agent decline is associated with a clean-up exercise but does not identify local service effects or customer harm.
observations.subgroup: Ghanaian mobile-money customers and agents in the regulated ecosystem.
observations.counterinterpretation: Removing fraudulent agents may improve trust and security even if the short-term active-agent count falls; low active/registered ratios do not directly measure dissatisfaction or exclusion.

denominator.unit: Bank of Ghana annual-report policy and oversight indicators; financial-access figure is a reported population access estimate, while licences and sanctions are institutional counts

financial_access_2021.unit: percent of the population reported as having access to financial services in the Bank’s 2021 milestone statement

fintech_license_growth.unit: percent growth in licensed fintech companies from 2023 to 2024

licensed_psps_fined.unit: licensed payment service providers fined during 2024 investigations

approved_digital_microloan_products.unit: digital micro-loan applications/products approved in 2024, compared with 1 in 2023

mechanism.value: Financial inclusion is jointly produced by access, active use, product authorization, agent integrity, consumer education, and enforcement; high headline access can coexist with an expanding risk-and-remedy workload

observations.method: Bank of Ghana annual-report administrative and policy indicators; the access estimate, licensing counts, approvals, and sanctions are not a single survey denominator and are intentionally kept distinct.
observations.uncertainty: The report’s access milestone is not equivalent to active usage, quality, affordability, consumer protection, or financial health; institutional counts do not measure outcomes for end users.
observations.subgroup: Ghanaian financial-service users, fintechs, PSPs, agents, and underserved populations addressed by the Bank’s inclusion interventions.
observations.counterinterpretation: More licences and sanctions can indicate stronger regulatory capacity rather than more underlying harm; digital lending approvals may expand useful access or increase future consumer risk depending on product conduct.

related_sources.claim: Bank of Ghana official landing page for the Payment Systems Oversight Annual Report 2024.
Bank of Ghana 2025 annual report retained as a future continuity source, not used for the 2024 observations in this record.

boundary: This record adds a Ghana administrative payment-system, agent-integrity, fintech-oversight, and financial-inclusion layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish unique-person use, household welfare, causal inclusion, consumer harm, cultural consumption, or the effect of sanctions and licensing on outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Bank of Ghana 45-page Payment Systems Oversight Annual Report 2024 reviewed; mobile-money system totals, registered/active customer and agent definitions, banking-channel growth, licensed fintechs, sanctions, financial-access milestone, and financial-inclusion caveats checked.
